import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture relating two characterizations of a set of integers.

Informal Statement:
For an integer $k \ge 2$, the following are equivalent:

1. The greatest common divisor of the binomial coefficients
    $\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.

2. Writing prime factorization of $k$ as
    $k = \prod p_i^{e_i}$, and let
    $P = \max_i p_i^{e_i}$,
    one has $k / P > P$.

This conjecture asserts that the sequence defined by 1. is obtained by
taking 1 off each number in the sequence defined by 2.

*References:*
- [A80170](https://oeis.org/A80170)
- [A51283](https://oeis.org/A51283)
-/

namespace OeisA80170

/--
The gcd of the binomial coefficients
$\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.
-/
def A (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (Finset.range k).gcd (fun i => Nat.choose ((i + 2) * k) k) = 1

/--
Let $P$ be the largest prime power dividing `k`.
Then $k / P > P$.
-/
def B (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let P := ((Nat.divisors k).filter IsPrimePow).max.getD 0
  k / P > P

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : ¬A 2 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : ¬A 3 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : ¬A 4 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : ¬A 5 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : ¬A 6 := by unfold A; decide

/--
Conjecture: The gcd condition is equivalent to the prime power condition.
This has been conjectured by Ralf Stephan.

Both the natural-language proof and its Lean 4 formalization were carried out
by the KLMM MechMath Agent Team; see the `formal_proof` attribute.

*References:*
- [Ralf Stephan, *Prove or Disprove. 100 Conjectures from the OEIS*, 2004, Conjecture 17 (arXiv:math/0409509)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409509)
- [Dakai Guo et al., *A Greatest Common Divisor Criterion of Certain Binomial Coefficients*, 2026 (arXiv:2606.22997)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22997)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/guodk/formal-conjectures/blob/0720658844d76a50d48e4baa152eef14d4462907/FormalConjectures/OEIS/80170.lean#L1823"]
theorem gcdCondition_iff_primePowerCondition (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    A k ↔ B (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA80170

findings.description: The module docstring (lines 23–31) claims that the gcd condition at k is equivalent to the prime-power condition at the same k. The source instead relates the gcd condition at k to the prime-power condition at k+1, as the Lean theorem correctly does. This distinction is substantive: A 29 is true, whereas B 29 is false (P = 29 and 29/P = 1); B 30 is true. The counterexample to the unshifted docstring was proved in scratch Lean without sorry or additional axioms. No theorem or definition needs changing.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A080170, Ralf Stephan's February 20, 2004 comment: “a(n) = A051283(n) - 1 (conjectured)” (https://oeis.org/A080170, read through the official oeis/oeisdata mirror). Guo et al., arXiv:2606.22997, Theorem 1, explicitly sets n = k+1 and states D(k)=1 iff n/ppart(n)>ppart(n).
findings.suggested_fix: Describe items 1 and 2 as two predicates, rather than as equivalent conditions at the same k, and explicitly assert that condition 1 at k is equivalent to condition 2 at k+1. Keep the following sequence-shift explanation and all Lean declarations unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The Lean takes the maximum of all prime-power divisors, rather than directly taking the maximum of the exact prime-power components in the factorization, and uses natural-number division rather than an ordinary rational quotient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n≥2 the filtered divisor set is nonempty. Every prime-power divisor p^j satisfies j≤n.factorization p, hence p^j≤p^(n.factorization p); conversely every exact component belongs to the filtered divisor set. Their maxima therefore coincide. This maximum P is positive and divides n, so natural division n/P is exact and its rational cast equals (n:ℚ)/(P:ℚ). The default maximum 0 is unreachable in the theorem, where n=k+1≥3. Both equality of the maxima and the equivalence with the source's rational inequality were proved in scratch Lean.

reformulations.difference: The OEIS conjecture is written as the termwise sequence relation A080170(n)=A051283(n)-1; Lean states the shifted membership equivalence ∀ k≥2, A k ↔ B (k+1).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both OEIS sequences increasingly enumerate the numbers satisfying their respective defining predicates. Subtracting 1 preserves the ordering of the second sequence, so the termwise relation is equivalent to the shifted equality of membership predicates. The omitted k=0,1 contribute no exceptions: A 0, A 1, B 1, and B 2 are all false, verified in Lean. Guo et al.'s Theorem 1 explicitly states the same shifted pointwise formulation as the Lean theorem. The full enumeration equivalence was not formalized; the finite-gcd reindexing and prime-power formula equivalences were.

review.notes:
All eight declarations were checked. The five test gcds are 3, 4, 5, 3, and 7; direct computation found no disagreement between A k and B (k+1) for k<100. Boundary cases and the docstring counterexample were kernel-checked. Final experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

The solved status is current: A080170's June 29, 2026 comment records Guo et al.'s proof. The cited external proof compiled after changing only its obsolete import path to FormalConjecturesUtil; its final theorem depends on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with no sorry or custom axioms, and its predicates are definitionally identical to the reviewed A and B.

Direct OEIS requests were blocked by Cloudflare, so the complete entries were read from OEIS's official data mirror. Stephan's 2004 equation (17) contains apparent typographical slips (a sum instead of a product and an endpoint (n−1)n); the original OEIS definitions and the precise 2026 theorem resolve the intended statement consistently. The reviewed file was not modified.
